# GitHub Flow and Trunk-Based Development

After this page you can contrast a short-lived PR branch with committing to `main` behind flags.

## GitHub Flow (as a Git topology)

```text
main          always deployable
feat/…        branched from main, opened as a PR, merged, deleted
```

There is no long-lived `develop`. Production is `main` (or a tag on it). CI on the PR is the gate.

```text
 GitHub Flow

 main     A ← B ← C ← M          always deployable
               ↖     ↗
 feat/ping      D ← E            PR, then delete
```

```bash
git switch main
git pull --ff-only
git switch -c feat/ping-json
# commits, push, PR, merge on the forge
git switch main
git pull --ff-only
git branch -d feat/ping-json
```

The name “GitHub Flow” is a topology. You can do it on Forgejo or GitLab. The forge UI is a PR/MR; Git is short-lived branches off `main`.

## Trunk-based

Engineers commit to `main` (the **trunk**) at least daily, often several times a day. Features that are not ready stay **dark** behind a flag (next page). Release branches, if any, are cut from `main` and live days, not months.

```text
 trunk-based

 main     A ← B ← C ← D ← E ← F     tiny commits, flags hide unfinished work
                     ╲
                      release/1.2   short-lived, if you even cut one
```

```bash
git switch main
# small commit
git pull --rebase
git push
```

Feature branches, when used, last hours. Rebase onto `main` before merge. `--ff-only` after a rebase is the usual integrate.

## Compare

| | Git Flow | GitHub Flow | Trunk-based |
|--|----------|-------------|-------------|
| Long-lived lines | `main` + `develop` | `main` | `main` |
| Feature lifetime | Days–weeks | Hours–days | Hours or a flag |
| Release | `release/*` branch | Tag / deploy `main` | Tag / short `release/*` |
| Fits | Multi-version products | Web apps, desk tools | High-CI teams |

`desk-api` in this book defaults to **GitHub Flow topology**: short `feat/` branches, `main` deployable. Trunk-based is the same graph with even shorter branches.

Enforcement (required reviews, required checks) is chapter 31. The next page is flags, which make trunk-based possible.
